notes: Access: curl_cffi chrome131 impersonation reached everything with HTTP 200 (plain fetch would likely 403 per prior notes for this host). Checked: robots.txt (no Claude-specific disallow), homepage full mega-nav (regex scan of every /catalog/* href across all 11 department trees: bath, bedroom, dining-and-kitchen, home-decor, lighting, living, made-for-you, office, outdoor, rugs, storage-and-entryway), each department root page's own sub-nav, footer links, the site's dedicated /catalog/sitemap page (425KB full category tree), and static.xml sitemap. Searched (English) for: Bestsellers, Best Sellers, Bestselling, Top Sellers, Popular, Most Popular, Customer Favorites, Trending -- zero matches anywhere in nav/sitemap/footer text or hrefs. The only superficially-similar hits were: /favorites (a personal saved-items/wishlist icon in the header, not a merchandising PLP), 'Seasonal Favorites' (a seasonal home-decor product category, unrelated to sales ranking), and 'Favorite Outdoor Dining Combos' / 'Favorite Outdoor Lounge Combos' (documentType=EDITORIAL curated pre-designed room-combo styling pages, not a bestseller/popularity listing) -- all excluded as non-matches to the Bestsellers concept. Also attempted the site's own search (/search?q=...) for 'best sellers' etc: the search page is client-rendered (SSR JSON only contains globalDynamicData, no results), so tried Playwright; this triggered a 'Just Checking' press-and-hold bot-detection challenge on the /search endpoint specifically -- first block encountered on this host, stopped per protocol rather than retrying with another method. This is a tooling/endpoint gap on the search feature only, not a full-site block (direct HTTP fetch of every catalog/department/sitemap page succeeded). Given the site is furniture-led with a conventional room/type-based catalog and Clearance is the only merchandising overlay found (see cl28.json), and no Bestsellers-branded page exists anywhere in nav or sitemap, concluding no genuine Bestsellers PLP exists on roomandboard.com.
